claims.title: The sacred landscape of Vat Phou
claims.summary: Around the Champasak plain in the south, a planned Hindu landscape develops around the Vat Phou temple, growing over a millennium largely under Khmer influence; it is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

sources.label: Vat Phou and Associated Ancient Settlements within the Champasak Cultural Landscape

claims.title: Tai-Lao settlement of the Mekong
claims.summary: Tai-speaking peoples migrating southward settle the middle Mekong valley, organizing into numerous small principalities (muang) such as Muang Swa, the future Luang Prabang.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-700-tai-lao-settlement-of-the-mekong, claim TL:LAO:event:700:tai-lao-settlement-of-the-mekong, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fa Ngum founds Lan Xang
claims.summary: Fa Ngum unifies the Lao principalities of the Mekong by conquest and proclaims the kingdom of Lan Xang, the "million elephants," with its capital at Muang Swa (Luang Prabang).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1353-fa-ngum-founds-lan-xang, claim TL:LAO:event:1353:fa-ngum-founds-lan-xang, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Theravada Buddhism established
claims.summary: During Fa Ngum's reign Theravada Buddhism of the Sinhalese school is introduced into the Lao kingdom, likely from Cambodia, becoming the foundational religion of Laos.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1353-theravada-buddhism-established, claim TL:LAO:event:1353:theravada-buddhism-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Setthathirath moves the capital to Vientiane
claims.summary: Facing Burmese pressure, King Setthathirath transfers his capital from Luang Prabang to Vientiane, brings the Emerald Buddha, and builds the great stupa of That Luang.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1560-setthathirath-moves-the-capital-to-vientiane, claim TL:LAO:event:1560:setthathirath-moves-the-capital-to-vientiane, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lan Xang splits apart
claims.summary: After a disputed succession, the kingdom of Lan Xang divides in 1707 into the separate kingdoms of Luang Prabang and Vientiane, ending its unity.

sources.label: Sai Ong Hue and the division of Lan Xang

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1707-lan-xang-splits-apart, claim TL:LAO:event:1707:lan-xang-splits-apart, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Champasak secedes
claims.summary: The far south breaks away to form the kingdom of Champasak, completing the fragmentation of Lan Xang into three rival Lao kingdoms.

sources.label: Sai Ong Hue and the division of Lan Xang

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1713-champasak-secedes, claim TL:LAO:event:1713:champasak-secedes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lao kingdoms become Siamese vassals
claims.summary: Divided and weakened, the rulers of Luang Prabang, Vientiane, and Champasak each fall under a Siamese commissioner and must pay tribute to Bangkok.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1779-the-lao-kingdoms-become-siamese-vassals, claim TL:LAO:event:1779:the-lao-kingdoms-become-siamese-vassals, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Siam destroys Vientiane
claims.summary: After King Anouvong's failed revolt against Bangkok, Siamese forces sack and raze Vientiane and deport its people, ending the kingdom of Vientiane.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1828-siam-destroys-vientiane, claim TL:LAO:event:1828:siam-destroys-vientiane, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French protectorate established
claims.summary: Following the Franco-Siamese crisis, Siam cedes the territory east of the Mekong and France makes the Lao states a protectorate within French Indochina, administered from Vientiane.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1893-french-protectorate-established, claim TL:LAO:event:1893:french-protectorate-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese occupation and the Lao Issara
claims.summary: Japan ousts the French administration in March 1945; after Japan's surrender, the nationalist Lao Issara (Free Lao) forms a provisional government to resist the return of French rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1945-japanese-occupation-and-the-lao-issara, claim TL:LAO:event:1945:japanese-occupation-and-the-lao-issara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Pathet Lao
claims.summary: Prince Souphanouvong breaks with the Lao Issara to ally with the Viet Minh and proclaims the communist-oriented Pathet Lao ("Land of the Lao"), the future ruling movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1950-founding-of-the-pathet-lao, claim TL:LAO:event:1950:founding-of-the-pathet-lao, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Full independence from France
claims.summary: The Franco-Lao Treaty of Amity and Association transfers the last French powers to the Royal Lao Government, recognizing Laos as a fully independent and sovereign state.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Laos
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Geneva agreement on Lao neutrality
claims.summary: An international agreement declares Laos neutral and provides for a coalition government, but the country remains a contested corridor of the Vietnam War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1962-geneva-agreement-on-lao-neutrality, claim TL:LAO:event:1962:geneva-agreement-on-lao-neutrality, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Secret War bombing
claims.summary: The United States drops more than two million tons of bombs on Laos to cut the Ho Chi Minh Trail, making it the most heavily bombed country per capita; vast unexploded ordnance remains a deadly legacy.

sources.label: Lao Special Guerrilla Unit and Royal Lao Army Veteran Interviews
U.S. Conventional Weapons Destruction Program in Lao PDR

claims.title: Paris accords and U.S. withdrawal
claims.summary: The Paris Peace Accords end direct American military involvement in Indochina, leaving the Lao factions to settle the civil war among themselves.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1973-paris-accords-and-u-s-withdrawal, claim TL:LAO:event:1973:paris-accords-and-u-s-withdrawal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Lao PDR
claims.summary: The Pathet Lao take power, abolish the 600-year-old monarchy, and proclaim the Lao People's Democratic Republic, with Souphanouvong as president and Kaysone Phomvihane as prime minister.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Laos
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: New Economic Mechanism reforms
claims.summary: Facing the failure of central planning, the ruling party launches market-oriented reforms, legalizing private enterprise and inviting foreign investment, echoing Vietnam's Doi Moi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1986-new-economic-mechanism-reforms, claim TL:LAO:event:1986:new-economic-mechanism-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Luang Prabang inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The former royal capital of Luang Prabang, a fusion of Lao and French colonial architecture at the meeting of the Mekong and Nam Khan, is added to the UNESCO World Heritage List.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1995-luang-prabang-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:LAO:event:1995:luang-prabang-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Laos joins ASEAN
claims.summary: The Lao PDR is admitted to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, cementing its integration into the region after decades of isolation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-1997-laos-joins-asean, claim TL:LAO:event:1997:laos-joins-asean, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Laos-China Railway opens
claims.summary: The 1,000-km railway linking Vientiane to Kunming begins operating, aiming to turn landlocked Laos into a land-linked hub of regional trade while deepening its debt to China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Laos: The Land of a Million Elephants, from the Mekong kingdom of Lan Xang through French Indochina and the most bombed nation on earth to a one-party socialist republic.", terralore.co/country/LAO/chronicle#ev-2021-laos-china-railway-opens, claim TL:LAO:event:2021:laos-china-railway-opens, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
